summary: Frontend re-test of the RevenueCat purchase flow after the identity-race fix. GOOD NEWS: The identity race is fixed — the paywall's Continue button becomes enabled instantly (aria-disabled=null) with a valid price ($79.99 annual / $9.99 monthly), no 'identity_not_ready' error surfaces, and the __DEV__ dev-confirm modal opens on tap. Rebrand verified: home title is 'NarcCheck AI', quota badge shows '3/3 FREE', paywall hero shows 'NARCCHECK AI PRO'. BAD NEWS: The completed RC Test Store purchase (log confirms `[Test store] Performing test purchase`) does NOT grant the `pro` entitlement, so isSubscribed never flips to true — the paywall stays open, the useEffect never calls router.back(), and the home screen never swaps quota-badge for pro-badge. The problem persists even after a full page reload, so the missing entitlement is on the RC server side (customerInfo.entitlements.active does not contain `pro`), not a stale client cache. Restore button tap works without crashing and surfaces no error. Backend testing was skipped per the frontend-only scope.

integration_issues.flow: Paywall Continue -> dev-confirm -> RC Test Store 'Test valid purchase' -> expected pro-badge on home
integration_issues.issue: RC Test Store purchase for product pro.annual completes successfully (console: '[Test store] Performing test purchase. This purchase won't appear in production.') but the resulting CustomerInfo does not include the `pro` entitlement under entitlements.active, so `isSubscribed` remains false. Because `isSubscribed` never flips, paywall.tsx's `useEffect(() => { if (isSubscribed) router.back(); })` never fires, the paywall stays open, and on returning to home the pro-badge is not shown (quota-badge remains). Reproduces even after a hard page reload, confirming the entitlement is genuinely absent on the RC user server-side — not a client-cache issue.

action_items: In the RevenueCat dashboard for the Test Store project, attach the `pro` entitlement to the `pro.monthly` and `pro.annual` products. Right now the test purchase completes but the returned CustomerInfo has an empty entitlements.active map, so the app has no way to detect a subscription. This is a dashboard-side config change, not code — but until it is done the E2E purchase acceptance criteria (paywall auto-closes, home shows PRO badge, Analyse bypasses paywall via subscription) cannot pass on web/test-store.

Defensive code hardening (optional but recommended): in /app/frontend/src/lib/revenuecat.tsx, make `purchaseMutation` and `restoreMutation` update the react-query cache directly instead of relying on `Purchases.addCustomerInfoUpdateListener` (that listener is not guaranteed to fire in RC web/Browser Mode). E.g. `onSuccess: (customerInfo) => queryClient.setQueryData(['revenuecat','customer-info'], customerInfo)` for purchaseMutation, and for restoreMutation, also `setQueryData` with the returned CustomerInfo. This closes any post-purchase cache-staleness path even before the RC dashboard fix.

Once the entitlement mapping is fixed in the RC dashboard, re-run this iteration's flow to confirm: (a) paywall closes on its own after the test purchase, (b) home switches to pro-badge, (c) Analyse with a valid transcript proceeds directly to /scorecard without hitting paywall.
critical_code_review_comments: revenuecat.tsx: The `enabled: rcEnabled && identityBound` gating on `customerInfoQuery` is a clean, minimal fix for the anonymous-overwrite race and verified working — no identity error, Continue button is enabled instantly, and identity check `identityReady` becomes true on paywall mount. Good fix.

revenuecat.tsx: `purchaseMutation` and `restoreMutation` do not directly update the react-query cache — they rely on `Purchases.addCustomerInfoUpdateListener`. In RC's web Browser Mode that listener may not fire reliably, and there's no explicit `queryClient.invalidateQueries` after purchase either. Recommend using `onSuccess` in the mutations to `setQueryData(['revenuecat','customer-info'], customerInfo)` as a belt-and-braces path.

paywall.tsx: The `canBuy = !!chosen && identityReady && !isPurchasing && !isRestoring` gate is correct; verified in flight — the button was tappable within ~0ms after paywall mount because customerInfoQuery had already been seeded by the logIn result.

paywall.tsx: dev-confirm overlay (`testID="dev-confirm-overlay"`) is well-scoped to __DEV__ and renders cleanly; the Cancel/Simulate buttons have appropriate min touch targets (12+16px paddingVertical on pill).

Rebranding is complete and consistent: app.json name is 'NarcCheck AI', home title is 'NarcCheck AI', locked CTA reads 'Unlock NarcCheck Pro', paywall hero badge reads 'NARCCHECK AI PRO', backend GET /api/ returns 'NarcCheck AI API online' (visible in source; not curled during this run per frontend-only scope).

success_rate.frontend: 7/8 acceptance criteria pass; 1 (post-purchase pro-badge on home) blocked by RC entitlement config

seed_data_creation: None. RC Test Store purchases are ephemeral and do not persist across the fresh anonymous device ids used per browser session.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Identity race is fixed and verified. Continue button enables instantly, dev-confirm modal opens, RC Test Store 'Test valid purchase' completes without error. The remaining blocker is entirely on the RC project config: the `pro` entitlement is not attached to the `pro.monthly` / `pro.annual` products in the Test Store, so CustomerInfo.entitlements.active stays empty after a successful test purchase. Fix path: (1) RC dashboard — attach `pro` entitlement to both products; (2) optional code hardening — make purchase/restore mutations call `queryClient.setQueryData(['revenuecat','customer-info'], customerInfo)` in onSuccess so client cache updates deterministically without relying on `addCustomerInfoUpdateListener` in Browser Mode. To re-verify: open paywall (quota badge tap) -> tap Continue -> tap Simulate in dev-confirm -> tap 'Test valid purchase' in RC modal -> paywall should auto-close within ~5s and home should show pro-badge (testID='pro-badge').
rca_of_issue: Root cause: RC Test Store purchase succeeds at the SDK level (product transaction recorded) but the resulting CustomerInfo does not report any active entitlement for the `pro` identifier the app is coded to check (REVENUECAT_ENTITLEMENT_IDENTIFIER = 'pro' in revenuecat.tsx). This is confirmed by the fact that a full page reload after the purchase still shows the quota badge, i.e. the entitlement is not present when re-fetched from RC servers — it is not a stale local cache. The most likely cause is that in the RC dashboard's Test Store project, the products pro.monthly and pro.annual are not linked to the `pro` entitlement. Once the entitlement mapping is added in the dashboard, the existing client code paths (`Purchases.addCustomerInfoUpdateListener` + the paywall's useEffect-on-isSubscribed router.back) should complete the acceptance flow; adding an explicit `queryClient.setQueryData` in the purchase mutation's onSuccess would make this deterministic in RC Browser Mode. Reproduction: (a) open http://<preview>/ -> quota-badge visible (3/3 FREE); (b) tap quota-badge -> paywall opens; (c) tap Continue -> dev-confirm-overlay opens; (d) tap dev-confirm -> RC modal 'Test Store Purchase' opens; (e) click 'Test valid purchase' -> RC console logs `[Test store] Performing test purchase`; (f) wait 10s -> paywall still visible, url still /paywall, pro-badge still absent; (g) hard-reload page -> quota-badge still shown, pro-badge still absent.
